answer.summary: It won't help your jumping, and a lot of static stretching right before jumping can lower power for a while. If you do stretch, keep it short and follow it with dynamic or ballistic work.

points.text: Static stretching doesn't make you jump higher. Right before speed-power work it temporarily lowers force and power, and the drop grows the more you stretch.
If you stretch in the warm-up, hold it about 30–60 seconds and follow it with something dynamic or ballistic. That largely cancels the brief power drop.
Stretch if you have mobility restrictions. If you don't want to stretch, you don't need to, because there's no longitudinal evidence that it helps speed-power athletes.
